stem: A team publishes its annual report as a PDF made from scanned page images. Which change makes the report accessible?

options.rationale: Scanned pages are images, so a screen reader has no text to read, real text plus tags and reading order make the content navigable.

options.text: Raise the scan resolution so the text looks sharper on screen.
options.rationale: Sharper images help magnification, but the page stays an image and a screen reader still cannot read it.

options.text: Add PDF bookmarks for each chapter and section.
options.rationale: Bookmarks speed navigation, but they do not expose the page text or its reading order to assistive technology.

options.text: Add a cover page that warns readers the PDF may be inaccessible.
options.rationale: A warning does not remove the barrier, the report's content still needs to be available as text.

explanation: A scan is a picture of text. Screen readers need actual characters and structure, so the document must be exported or rebuilt as a tagged PDF with a logical reading order, or offered in an accessible HTML format. Higher resolution, bookmarks, and warnings do not make the text readable.
author: Oxypteros
